text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel switch (kts-12) we're seeing p95 spikes on /generate-chat for high-priority routes (tier=gold). +40-60ms vs baseline, started ~02:30 UTC. Anyone else noticing?

ci-bot: deploy succeeded: runtime-kernel-v12 -> prod @2145671200 (canary 10% -> 100%)

ajay: saw an alert. Do you have the p95 numbers and a short perf sample? :eyes:

maria: quick numbers: p50 60ms, p95 210ms (was ~165ms), p99 unchanged. Sampled a few requests, attached stack-ish profile below.

```
route: /generate-chat
model: llm-a1
seq_len: 512
microbatch distribution: [1: 35%, 2: 40%, 4: 20%, 8:5%]
kv_hit_ratio: 0.68
profile (wall ms): kernel_dispatch 12, attention_kernel 48->72 (+24), kv_prefetch 3, scheduling_overhead 6->20 (+14)
```

zli: interesting — attention kernel time jumped. Could be a kernel choice fallback for certain seq shapes. Did the kernel selector change heuristics with the new compile flags?

ajay: yes, kts-12 introduced heuristic to prefer fused-attn for short heads but added a pessimistic path for some threadblocks. Might be triggering for seq=512 microbatches >4.

samir: is batching/queueing different? If we see more microbatches of 4 and 8 that could push attention into the slower path. What's queue policy token budget for gold?

maria: current runtime config snippet:

```json
{
  "queue_policy": "slo_aware",
  "token_budgets_by_tier": {"gold": "auto", "silver": 80, "bronze": 50},
  "dynamic_allocator": {
    "mode": "p95_target",
    "p95_ms": 200,
    "prefetch_kv": true
  }
}
```

zli: hmm token_budgets_by_tier gold=auto => allocator probably bumped budgets to keep p95 but that should reduce microbatching, not increase it. The scheduling_overhead jump suggests queue shaper hysteresis or kernel switchover thrash.

ajay: can you run the perf harness with sampling that prints kernel selection decisions? e.g.

```bash
tools/perf/harness --route /generate-chat --duration 120 --qps 80 --seq 512 --sample-kernel-decisions > sample.log
```

maria: running now on canary nodes, I'll paste sample.log if it reproduces.

ci-bot: perf-harness job started on canary group cg-4 (job id ph-2145678901-1)

maria: sample.log excerpt:

```
req 10234: microbatch=4 -> selected_kernel=fused_attn_fast (edges: no)
req 10235: microbatch=8 -> selected_kernel=fallback_blocked_attn (edges: yes)
req 10241: microbatch=2 -> fused_attn_fast
req 10287: microbatch=4 -> fallback_blocked_attn  # extra branch taken when head_dim=64 and threads>32
```

zli: that matches my hypothesis. New kernel selector's thresholds are too tight for our head_dim distribution. We should either relax switchover or force preferring the previous kernel for seq>=256 and microbatch<=8.

ajay: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback kts-12 for prod canary (fast, but loses other perf wins), 2) adjust selector config (thresholds) and push a tiny config-only rollout, 3) tune dynamic allocator to bias toward smaller token budgets for gold so fewer microbatches hit the slow path.

samir: (3) seems least risky. If gold token budget reduces, we'll bias toward more single-request microbatches which look like they pick fused_attn_fast. But cost/throughput tradeoff.

maria: I can try (3) first: set token_budgets_by_tier.gold=100 (instead of auto) and lower early_cutoff to 6ms. Will test on canary 10% and watch p95.

ops-bot: scheduled config roll: runtime-config -> canary-10% in 5m (change id cfg-2145678901-2)

ajay: please also collect kernel-decision histograms and per-microbatch latency buckets during canary. If p95 improves without impacting throughput, we keep. If not, rollback to kts-11.

maria: agreed. Running now. Will post metrics and the short decision histogram in ~10m. :thumbsup:

zli: also open a short follow-up PR to make the selector thresholds data-driven: add a small telemetry export of head_dim vs microbatch decision counts. That would prevent regressing like this in future. :eyes:

maria: filed ticket RW-6821 and PR draft linked in canary thread. Will update with numbers.

maria: quick update (canary metrics): p95 -> 168ms (back near baseline), throughput -1.8%, cost delta +2.4% for canary traffic. kernel decision histogram shows 72% fused_attn_fast vs 28% fallback.

ajay: looks acceptable as short-term fix. We should keep selector change in a feature branch and iterate on thresholds. Plan: keep config change, revert kernel change on next full deploy candidate until selector is hardened.

maria: plan noted. Closing this thread once rollback window passes. Thanks all. :sparkles:
